coverage_notes: A04 Insecure Design is out of scope. DVWA is a teaching app; findings describe vulnerability classes, not attack recipes.

findings.title: SQL query built from request parameters
findings.description: DVWA's SQL injection lesson concatenates request data into SQL. That is a textbook injection flaw used for teaching, not a production scanner payload.
findings.evidence: Catalog finding for DVWA. WebSET does not submit injection strings.
findings.recommendation: Use prepared statements with bound parameters. Disable detailed database errors in responses.

findings.title: Command execution lesson exposes unsanitised OS input
findings.description: The command-injection module passes user input toward an OS command. This demo records the class of issue DVWA is designed to illustrate.
findings.evidence: Catalog finding. No operating-system commands are issued by the scanner.
findings.recommendation: Never pass request data to a shell. If a system tool must run, use a fixed command array and an allow-list of arguments.

findings.title: Cross-site scripting lesson reflects unsanitised input
findings.description: Reflected XSS modules echo input back into HTML. The finding is the encoding gap, not a working payload.
findings.recommendation: Context-encode output. Enable a CSP that disallows inline script in production systems.

findings.title: File upload accepts executable content types
findings.description: The upload exercise stores files with weak type and path checks. Combined with a web-reachable upload directory this becomes remote code execution in real apps.
findings.evidence: Catalog finding. WebSET does not upload files.
findings.recommendation: Allow only expected MIME types and extensions, store uploads outside the web root, and serve them with a fixed content-type.

findings.title: Default training credentials remain enabled
findings.description: DVWA ships with well-known lab credentials. That is appropriate for a classroom and unacceptable on any network-exposed system.
findings.evidence: Catalog finding. Credentials are not tested or stored.
findings.recommendation: Force unique passwords on first boot for any non-lab deployment. Disable default accounts.

findings.title: Security headers are absent on lab responses
findings.description: A live header pass typically finds no CSP, nosniff, or framing policy on DVWA.
findings.evidence: Live header inspection when reachable; otherwise catalog default.
findings.recommendation: Add security headers at the reverse proxy or application layer. Do not expose DVWA beyond localhost.

findings.title: PHP and server versions are disclosed
findings.description: Version banners help an analyst inventory the stack. They also help attackers choose known-vulnerable builds.
findings.recommendation: Suppress version banners. Keep PHP and extensions current via the OS package manager or image rebuilds.

findings.title: CSRF protections are optional in the lesson modules
findings.description: State-changing requests in the CSRF module can be issued without a per-session token depending on the selected security level.
findings.recommendation: Require anti-CSRF tokens on cookie-authenticated state changes, and consider SameSite cookie attributes.

findings.title: Lab security level is a configuration risk if left at low
findings.description: DVWA lets an instructor lower protections to make flaws obvious. That is useful in class and dangerous if the container is reachable beyond the lab.
findings.recommendation: Bind the container to localhost only. Treat security level as a teaching control, not a production setting.
